Request for the Commission to grant authority to the Department of Housing to negotiate a redevelopment agreement with Mercy Housing Lakefront for the redevelopment of the property located at 1207 W. Leland Ave. in the Lawrence/Broadway Redevelopment Project Area, and for the Commission to recommend to the City Council the designation of Mercy Housing Lakefront as Developer.

Request for the Commission to grant authority to the Department of Planning and Development to negotiate a redevelopment agreement with Chicago Neighborhood Initiatives for the redevelopment of the property located at 758 E. 111th St. in the North Pullman Redevelopment Project Area, and for the Commission to recommend to the City Council the designation of Chicago Neighborhood Initiatives as Developer.

A proposed Planned Development, submitted by MKR Owner LLC for the property generally located at 1133 W. Kinzie Street . The Applicant requests a rezoning of the subject property from M2-3 to DX-5 to construct a 5-story, 59’-11” residential building with a maximum number of 110 dwelling units, 33 car parking spaces and a maximum FAR of 5.

A proposed amendment to Institutional Planned Development 108, submitted by Chicago Realty Ventures, LLC, for the property generally located at 3700-3846 N Seminary Avenue, 1100-1156 W Grace Street, and 3801-3851 N Racine Avenue . The applicant proposes amending Planned Development 108 to extend the boundaries of the Planned Development and establish three subareas. The existing surface parking lot in Subarea A is proposed to include up to 800 parking stalls as previously granted via minor change on March 4, 2014. No changes are proposed to Subarea B, which contains an existing public park. Subarea C will include an existing surface parking lot with up to 103 parking spaces. The proposed maximum Floor Area Ratio (FAR) of all subareas is 1.2.

A resolution seeking the adoption of the South Chicago Land Use Framework plan. This planning effort led by DPD establishes a framework for future land use recommendations in the South Chicago community area in the 7 th and 10 th wards. It evaluated land use, zoning, community priorities, and redevelopment opportunities in South Chicago, informed by a public engagement process and review of community-led planning initiatives. The recommendations of the land use framework will serve as a planning tool to support strengthening residential areas, foster thriving commercial corridors, and open spaces, and achieve other local priorities
